description_full: Yesway, Inc. owns and operates convenience stores in the United States. The company's store offers packaged bakery items, bottled water, salty snacks, bagged candy, jerky, chips, milk, bread, eggs, packaged beverages, meat snacks, chocolate, and nuts. It also offers food services, including deep-fried burritos. In addition, its store offers other ancillary services, including cash ATMs, crypto-currency ATMs, money orders, gift cards, propane tanks, in-store gaming, Amazon Lockers, lottery tickets, and other non-consumable products. It operates under two brands, Yesway and Allsup's. The company was founded in 2015 and is based in Fort Worth, Texas.
ceo_bio: Mr. Thomas Nicholas Trkla | Founder, Chairman, CEO & President | Age 65 | Compensation: $4.1M (FY2025)
financial_summary: Yesway, Inc. is a small-cap consumer defensive business with a $770M market cap on $2.7B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +3% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.

Returns on capital run at 6% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 20% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $46M in free cash flow — roughly 2 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 13.03× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 5.9× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 1.6× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 1.2%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 4.0% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
